target.title: fix(process): add gemini and claude to Windows .cmd shim allowlist
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- On Windows, using the `google-gemini-cli` provider fails with `spawn gemini ENOENT` because Node's `child_process.spawn` does not automatically resolve `.cmd` extensions (only `.exe`/`.com`)
- npm global installs on Windows create `.cmd` shim files, so `gemini` (and `claude`) need the `.cmd` suffix to be found by `spawn`
- Fixes #98573

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor child adapter (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`) has a `resolveCommand` function that uses `resolveWindowsCommandShim` with a hardcoded allowlist of commands that should get `.cmd` appended on Windows. The list included `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, and `npx` but not `gemini` or `claude` — so spawning those CLI tools failed on Windows.

## What Was Changed

- Added `gemini` and `claude` to the `cmdCommands` allowlist in `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts:26`
- This triggers the same `.cmd` resolution + `cmd.exe` wrapping mechanism already used and verified for `pnpm`, `yarn`, `npm`, and `npx`

## Scope

This PR is intentionally narrow: **allowlist-only**. The shared `cmd.exe` metacharacter escaping change has been split out to a follow-up PR to keep the shell-boundary review separate from the shim resolution fix.

## User Impact

- Windows users can now use the `google-gemini-cli` and `claude-cli` providers without encountering `ENOENT` spawn errors
- No change on macOS or Linux (platform guard already skips non-Windows)
- No change to the shared `cmd.exe` escaping path (metacharacter rejection behavior is unchanged)

## Evidence

### Real Windows Machine (MINGW64, Node.js v22.19.0)

**Bug:** `spawn("gemini") -> ENOENT`, `spawn("gemini.cmd") -> EINVAL` (CVE-2024-27980)  
**Fix:** `cmd.exe /d /s /c "gemini.cmd --version" -> exit 0`

### npm package evidence
`@google/gemini-cli` declares `{"gemini":"bundle/gemini.js"}` -> Windows npm creates `gemini.cmd`

### CI evidence
- `checks-windows-node-test` on `windows-latest`: all process tests pass on real Windows
- All unit tests pass via `setPlatform("win32")` simulation

## Tests

```bash
pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts  # 21 tests, 20 pass (1 pre-existing Linux failure)
pnpm test src/process/windows-command.test.ts  # 4 tests pass
```

New tests added:
- `wraps gemini CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows (#98573)` — verifies `gemini` -> `gemini.cmd` wrapped via `cmd.exe`
- `wraps claude CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows` — same for `claude`
- `keeps gemini command unchanged on non-Windows platforms (#98573)` — verifies no `.cmd` suffix on Linux

## Risk checklist

- [x] No: Does this change affect user-visible behavior? (Only affects Windows CLI tool spawning, restoring expected behavior)
- [x] No: Does this change affect configuration surface?
- [x] No: Does this change affect security? (No change to security model; same allowlist pattern used for other CLI tools like pnpm/npm/yarn)
- [x] No: Does this change affect plugin APIs?
- [x] No: Does this change require documentation updates?
